Draw the nomogram, and prove it agrees with the model

Source: R/nomogram.R
mm_nomogram.Rd

Builds the canonical rms::nomogram() from the exact fitted model, with the same datadist it was fitted under, then reads the drawn nomogram back the way a clinician reads it and checks that the answer matches mm_predict().

Usage

mm_nomogram(
  model,
  out_dir = NULL,
  tolerance = 1e-06,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  fun_at = NULL,
  funlabel = "Predicted risk",
  labels = NULL,
  level_case = c("title", "asis"),
  id = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A mm_model().

out_dir

Directory for the exported files. NULL draws nothing.

tolerance

Largest absolute difference in predicted risk tolerated between the nomogram and mm_predict() at tabulated values.

width, height

Inches. NULL, the default, sizes the sheet to the model: a nomogram's rows do not get shorter when there are more of them, so a page of fixed height crushes a model with many predictors into an unreadable sheet. The ENT applicant model, 27 axes on the 9 inches that suited 3, printed row labels across their own tick marks.

fun_at

Risk ticks for the printed risk axis.

funlabel

The printed risk axis's own label. Not every model this package fits predicts a risk: the same machinery drew a nomogram for the chance of matching into a residency, where "Predicted risk" is the wrong noun on a sheet handed to the person it is about.

labels

Printed names for the predictor axes, as a named character vector. The usual way to set these is Hmisc::label() on the cohort before fitting, which rms carries into the drawn sheet on its own; this argument is for relabelling a model that is already fitted. Renaming happens after the sheet has been checked against mm_predict() and never before, so the check matches axes to predictors by the names the fit gave them and a printed name cannot change what was verified.

level_case

What to do with the level text a categorical axis prints. Levels arrive as they were typed into a data-entry form, so a published sheet carries no AOA at school down the middle of the page. "title", the default, title cases them for printing and leaves a word carrying a capital of its own alone, so AOA and USMLE survive. "asis" prints them exactly as the fit holds them. Like labels, this happens after the sheet has been checked and never before.

id

Optional text appended to the exported filenames, as <slug>_nomogram_<id>.pdf. Two fits of the same project otherwise write the same three filenames, and the export refuses to overwrite, so this is how both sheets reach disk. A run id, a date, or whatever distinguishes the fits; it is used verbatim.

Value

An object of class mm_nomogram. Its nomogram element is the sheet that was checked, carrying the levels the fit holds; drawn is the copy that was printed, with any renaming and title casing applied.

Details

A nomogram that disagrees with the model it was drawn from is worse than no nomogram, because it is a published instrument giving wrong risks. So the agreement is asserted rather than assumed, which is what the specification's nomogram contract requires.

The check is made at the nomogram's own tabulated tick values, where agreement holds to machine precision. Reading between ticks is a different matter: a spline term curves between printed ticks and linear interpolation across them does not, so an off-tick reading carries the axis's resolution error. That is a property of every printed nomogram and of the clinician reading it, not a defect here. reading_error bounds it: no reading between the printed ticks can differ from mm_predict() by more than that figure. See mm_reading_error() for how a bound is reached without searching the joint space, and for the three things it does not cover.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
project <- mm_project("uds", "event", c("age", "bmi", "sex"),
                      cohort = cohort)
fit <- mm_model(project, cohort, nonlinear = "age")
#> Warning: the development sample may be too small for this model: 300 rows is 22175 short of the 22475 a model of 5 parameter(s) needs at 9.3% prevalence for 90% shrinkage. Coefficients from a sample this size are expected to be overfitted; see the adequacy element of the returned object.
nom <- mm_nomogram(fit, out_dir = NULL)
nom
#> <mm_nomogram>
#>   axes            age, bmi, sex
#>   profiles checked 20 at tabulated ticks
#>   worst gap vs mm_predict() 5.55e-17 (tolerance 1e-06)
#>   between-tick reading      0.00881 in risk at most, anywhere off the ticks
#>                             age is the coarsest axis
